findings.title: Route validation to the resolved worktree
findings.description: The command discards `worktreeId` and always validates `project.projectPath`. From a registered worktree, no-path validation checks—and `--fix` modifies—the main checkout instead. Explicit worktree paths are rejected by the service’s containment filter, potentially reporting zero files checked. Use `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)` and add worktree-routing tests.

findings.title: Revalidate before declaring fixes successful
findings.description: `remaining` contains only initially unfixable or failed findings, not the document’s actual post-fix findings. The schema validator returns immediately when `docType` is missing. Consequently, fixing an inferred `docType` exits successfully even when required fields remain missing. Revalidate modified files before determining the exit code; test a document initially missing `docType` and other required fields.

findings.title: Preserve process-event handler compatibility
findings.description: `index.ts` registers `handleError` directly for `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection`. Those events supply an origin string or Promise as their second argument, which now becomes `exitCode`. Reproduced both paths on Node 22: `process.exit()` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`, adding a secondary crash to error reporting. Wrap the listeners with single-argument callbacks and test both event paths.

findings.title: Do not overwrite the write-date stamp with a stale backfill
findings.description: For a document missing both `status` and `dateUpdated`, validation generates a status fix followed by a `dateUpdated = dateCreated` fix. The first write stamps today, but the second overwrites it with the historical creation date because the writer treats an explicit `dateUpdated` value as authoritative. Use the run’s date for that fix and add a multi-finding test.
